blocks.text: 1. ScaNN

blocks.alt: Partitioning leads to anisotropic quantization, then rescoring

blocks.text: ScaNN covers a search technique that combines several optimization tricks together, showing how earlier ideas can be layered rather than chosen between.
It layers partitioning, scoring, and reordering steps into one combined pipeline.
2. One Algorithm Versus A Combined Pipeline
Every algorithm covered so far relied on one dominant technique: a graph, clusters, or hashing.
ScaNN instead combines multiple techniques together into one search pipeline.

blocks.text: 3. The Partitioning Step In ScaNN
Much like the clustering step in IVF, ScaNN starts with a clustering style partitioning step.
This narrows the candidate set before any deeper scoring work begins.
4. Scoring With Approximate Distances

blocks.alt: A query computes an approximate score to produce a candidate set

blocks.text: Similar to the approximate distance reconstruction in Product Quantization, candidates within selected partitions get scored using fast, compressed distance estimates.
This avoids full precision comparisons for the large initial candidate pool.
5. Rescoring Top Candidates

blocks.alt: A candidate set is exactly rescored to produce the final top-K

blocks.text: Only a small final shortlist gets a more precise, full precision distance recalculation.
This spends accuracy effort only where it matters most: on the results likely to be returned.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: ScaNN's three stage pipeline narrows millions of vectors down to a small candidate set, then scores that set cheaply, and finally re-verifies only the very best candidates with full precision.

blocks.text: 6. Anisotropic Vector Quantization

blocks.alt: Standard quantization is compared against anisotropic quantization optimized for search

blocks.text: ScaNN uses a specialized quantization approach that weighs errors differently depending on their direction.
This prioritizes accuracy along the directions that matter most for ranking correctness.
7. Why Combining Techniques Helps
Much like the IVF versus HNSW comparison, each individual technique has its own strengths and weaknesses.
Stacking complementary techniques lets ScaNN often outperform any single approach alone.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A single technique like clustering alone, as in IVF, leaves accuracy on the table that a combined pipeline like ScaNN recovers by adding cheap scoring and precise rescoring stages on top.

blocks.text: 8. Engineering Complexity Tradeoff
Combining multiple stages means more moving parts to configure and tune correctly.
That complexity is the real cost behind ScaNN's strong benchmark performance.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When ScaNN Is Worth Its Added Complexity

blocks.alt: Needing top-tier accuracy and speed points toward ScaNN

blocks.text: Large scale systems needing top tier speed and recall justify ScaNN's complexity.
Simpler pipelines needing straightforward setup may prefer a single technique like HNSW or IVF alone.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates a simplified three stage pipeline mirroring ScaNN's partition, score, and rescore approach.

code.content:
import random

def euclidean_distance(v1, v2):
    return sum((a - b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(v1, v2)) ** 0.5

def fake_fast_score(query, vector):
    # a cheap approximation, comparing only the first few dimensions
    return euclidean_distance(query[:4], vector[:4])

def scann_style_search(query, vectors, num_partitions_to_check=3, shortlist_size=10, final_k=3):
    partition_size = len(vectors) // num_partitions_to_check
    candidates = vectors[:partition_size * num_partitions_to_check]

    scored = sorted(range(len(candidates)), key=lambda i: fake_fast_score(query, candidates[i]))
    shortlist = scored[:shortlist_size]

    rescored = sorted(shortlist, key=lambda i: euclidean_distance(query, candidates[i]))
    return rescored[:final_k]

vectors = [[random.random() for _ in range(16)] for _ in range(1000)]
query = [random.random() for _ in range(16)]

final_results = scann_style_search(query, vectors)
print(f"Total vectors in collection: {len(vectors)}")
print(f"Final rescored top results: {final_results}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows a large candidate pool getting narrowed by cheap partitioning and approximate scoring before only the final shortlist receives a precise recalculation.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Treating ScaNN as a single simple technique rather than understanding its multi stage pipeline.
Skipping the final rescoring stage, leaving results based only on cheap approximate scores.
Underestimating the configuration complexity that comes with combining multiple search stages.
Choosing ScaNN for a simple pipeline where a single technique would have been sufficient.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: ScaNN layers partitioning, scoring, and reordering steps into one combined search pipeline.
Unlike earlier algorithms relying on one dominant technique, ScaNN combines multiple approaches.
It starts with an IVF style partitioning step to narrow the candidate set.
Candidates within selected partitions get scored using fast, compressed distance estimates.
Only a small final shortlist gets a precise, full precision distance recalculation.
A specialized anisotropic quantization approach weighs errors by their direction, not uniformly.
Combining complementary techniques lets ScaNN often outperform any single approach alone.
That combination comes with more moving parts to configure and tune correctly.
